review.subject: Ceramic tableware collections laid out as top-down table settings
review.summary: Four ceramic dinnerware sets are each assembled from a blank cream surface by hands placing pieces, then labelled with a numbered title. It is a locked-off overhead shot with hand entrances and hard cuts between collections.

beats.note: Blank surface, hand places first bowl, set 1 appears fully styled.
Set 1 held static with numbered title, then hand cut to set 2.
Set 2 white and gold place pieces, held static.
Sets 3 and 4 follow the same hand place then title formula.

shot_labels.note: Blank cream surface, handheld drift, hand enters
Set 1 dark glazed pieces with numbered title
Hand rushes in carrying a plate, fast pan
Set 2 white and gold set, static
Hand with pieces sliding out, handheld
Hand drags tray in, quick pan
Set 4 blue glazed, static with title

learn: Shoot top-down locked off; reveal each set with a 1.6-1.9s static hold so the layout can be read.
Cut from blank to full table with a hand entrance (0.7-1.0s) to signal each new item.
Overlay a small numbered title at the top for every collection, same position and style.
Use pale neutral background and vary only plate colour for easy comparison across sets.
Handheld jitter only on hand-entry shots; keep hero holds fully static.
